knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A record with before-and-after photographs, the method, the product and the time gives evidence of what was done and what was observed.
A template reduces repeated admin while keeping evidence consistent. It does not remove the checks, and it does not hide exclusions or defects.
A written handover states what was done, what was excluded and any defect referred. A verbal compliance assurance or an energy promise is not acceptable.
An electrical or structural concern is escalated in writing to the owner and a qualified person. Keeping it quiet, fixing it on the spot or deleting a photo is not acceptable.
A template with fields for scope, exclusions, approvals and defects, reviewed by a person, reduces workload without removing checks. Auto-approval or hidden defects are not acceptable.

practicalCriteria: The learner completes a supplied job record with owner, approvals, scope, exclusions, method and photographs.
The learner writes a customer handover that states what was done, what was excluded and what is referred, with no guarantee.
The learner marks unknown or not-applicable fields rather than leaving them blank.
The learner adds a correction as a dated entry and does not delete or alter a photograph or record.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is assessed separately on a completed job record. A knowledge pass does not verify record quality on real jobs.
evidenceRequired: Completed job record with owner, approvals, scope, exclusions, method and photographs
Written customer handover with exclusions and referrals
Escalation log with the person told and the date
stopWorkCriteria: The learner writes a compliance or performance guarantee in a handover.
The learner deletes or alters a photograph or record.
The learner leaves an exclusion or defect out of the record.
The learner uses a template that auto-approves work without checking it.
